intervention.label: New farm pond
intervention.about: A farm pond or headwater pond that first holds water in a year from 2019 and keeps holding water in most years since. Most are dug on private farmland (MGNREGA, state farm-pond schemes such as Magel Tyala Shettale, or by farmers) to store runoff for protective irrigation.

years.about: Hydrological years (2019 = 2019-20). A pond is new if its first wet year is between first_appearance and last_appearance; 2017 and 2018 are kept as pre years. Effects in years up to last_main are identified by ponds not yet built in the same district and year; later years (2023-24) have few such ponds left and are reported as early signs.

appearance.about: New ponds must be wet in at least persist_share of the years from their first wet year. A pre year counts (qualifying pre year) only if at least neighbour_wet_share of the established waterbodies of the same home MWS (same type if there are same_type_min of them, else any type; at least min_neighbours) were wet that year and it was not a drought year: a dry pre year in a wet landscape means the pond was not there yet, not that it was dry. Ponds without a qualifying pre year are not assessed. A first wet year of 2019 may also be an older pond that was dry in the drought years 2017-18, so these are flagged.

drought.about: A drought year in the home MWS has 4 or more weeks of moderate or severe kharif drought (CoRE Stack kharif drought data; the Drought Manual's 3-4 week dry-spell trigger), as in the waterbody atlas.

outcomes.label: Cropping intensity
outcomes.about: Cropping intensity of the pond's zone of influence (ZoI, the cropland around it that CoRE Stack links to it), in percentage points: 100 is one crop a year on all cropland.

outcomes.label: Rabi and summer cropping
outcomes.about: Share of the ZoI's cropland under a crop outside the monsoon (rabi or summer), in percentage points: the season a stored-water pond should help.

outcomes.label: Multi-cropped share
outcomes.about: Double and triple cropped share of the cropped area, in percentage points.

outcomes.label: Cropped share
outcomes.about: Share of the ZoI's cropland cropped at least once in the year, in percentage points.

footprint.about: A pond dug on cropland takes that land out of cultivation. After construction the ZoI outcomes measured over its cropable area are divided by (1 - pond area / ZoI area), capped at max_share, so the pond's own footprint is not counted as a loss of cropping.

background.about: The comparison series is the home MWS's own cropping, computed without the ZoI cropland of every waterbody that appeared from 2019, so the effect of new ponds is not counted as background change. Overlapping zones can add up to more than the MWS's cropland, so at most max_remove of it is removed.

estimators.label: Imputation (headline)
estimators.about: Fitted on the years before each pond was built (and on ponds not yet built): pond baseline + year effect for the district + the MWS background outcome + drought weeks. The fitted model predicts each built pond's outcome had it not been built; the effect is observed minus predicted. A district-year with fewer than min_cell not-yet-built ponds falls back to the year effect over all districts, and then to the background alone (marked background support).

estimators.label: Same-district DiD
estimators.about: Each cohort (ponds first wet in the same year) against ponds of the same district not yet built by that year, change from the mean of the pre years; with no covariates, with pond size, ZoI size, catchment and stream order, and adding the MWS background level, its change and drought weeks (doubly robust: a propensity model and an outcome model). Weighted by the number of ponds in each cohort and year.

estimators.label: Change against the MWS background
estimators.about: The pond's ZoI minus its MWS background, after construction minus before. Uses no other ponds; reported as a check on the sign of each pond's effect.

estimators.label: Placebo: the year before construction
estimators.about: The imputation model refitted without each pond's last pre year, which is then predicted as if it were a post year. A real effect should not appear before the pond did.

lining.about: Many farm ponds, especially in Maharashtra, are lined with plastic sheet and are filled from wells as well as from runoff, so they store water for rabi and summer crops; unlined ponds lose water to seepage, recharge groundwater and mostly hold water in the monsoon. Lining is not observed, so the class is read from the water seen after the pond first holds water. Lined-like: water in summer (zaid) in at least lined_summer_years of those years, over at least lined_summer_area % of its area, and at least min_supporting of the supporting signs. Unlined-like: summer water on less than unlined_summer_area % of its area, with neither a drought-proof fill nor more water in rabi or summer than in kharif. Supporting signs: kharif fill in drought years at least drought_fill_ratio of that in normal years (filled by pumping, not only by rain), rabi or summer water above the kharif water, and a steady kharif fill (coefficient of variation below steady_cv). Everything else is uncertain. The class describes how the pond behaves, not how it was built; it is used only for the impact assessment and the waterbody's note, not as a type or role.

verdict.about: A pond's effect (mean over its post years up to last_main) is placed among the means of as many placebo residuals of ponds before they were built (no-pond years). At or above percentile gain_pct: likely gain; at or below percentile loss_pct: likely loss; provided its own placebo residual lies within the placebo_band percentile band and is smaller than the effect, and the background check agrees in sign; otherwise inconclusive. In between: no detectable change. With fewer than min_post_years_full years, or only years after last_main, a gain or loss is an early sign.

averages.about: Averages of the ponds' effects (years up to last_main) with a 95% bootstrap range over ponds, for each district, tehsil and micro-watershed, and by lined/unlined class. Units with fewer than min_n ponds are shown with a caution.

heterogeneity.about: Which ponds gain most: a random forest is fitted to the ponds' effects on landscape and pond features (without the pond's own pre-construction ZoI cropping, which would only pick up regression to the mean), cross-fitted over folds, and tested with the best linear predictor (BLP), sorted-group averages (GATES) and the features of the top and bottom groups (CLAN).

effectiveness.about: Structures wet since 2017 cannot be compared before and after. For them the atlas reports the gap between cropping intensity in the ZoI and in the home MWS, minus the site premium: the same gap at sites in the same district where waterbodies of the same type were built later, measured before they were built. It is a cross-sectional measure that assumes older structures were sited like newer ones, not a causal estimate.

farm_pond.label: new farm ponds
farm_pond.note: 561 new farm ponds in Pune district raised cropping intensity in their zones of influence by about 2.4 points on average (95% range +0.8 to +4.1), compared with the prediction had they not been built. 82 show a likely gain or an early sign of one and 63 a loss, against about 56 each expected by chance. Ponds whose water looks lined: +3.0 points (207 ponds); unlined: −2.8 points (70). Rabi and summer cropping changed by −1.0 points of the zones' cropland. In 2023-24 and 2024-25, with only the micro-watersheds left as comparison, the 686 ponds with data in those years show +5.2 points (an early sign).

panel._about: Fixed text of the new-farm-pond panels and of the Impact assessment tab's farm-pond tables (web/index.html, fpT). Text is shown as written; placeholders in braces are filled by the page.

panel.waterbody_eyebrow: Impact of a new farm pond
panel.row_placebo: Placebo: the year before it first held water
panel.row_percentile: Percentile among ponds in the years before they were built
panel.lining_detail: Water after it first filled: summer water in {summer_years}% of years, over {summer_area}% of its area on average; rabi water {rabi}%, kharif {kharif}%; fill in drought ÷ normal years {fill_ratio}.
panel.method_note: The prediction comes from the pond's own years before it was built, ponds in {district} district not yet built in the same year, the cropping of its micro-watershed (leaving out the fields around other new ponds) and kharif drought weeks. Outcomes after construction are corrected for the cropland the pond itself occupies.
panel.flag_appeared_2019: first wet in 2019-20 after the dry years 2017-18, so it may be an older pond
panel.flag_small: under 0.1 ha, where the water classifier is least reliable
panel.chart_aria: Cropping intensity in the zone of influence, its micro-watershed and the prediction without the pond
panel.waterbody_footer: New ponds are found from the water series: there is no registry. The effect is observed cropping minus the prediction had the pond not been built, and it is placed among the same differences for ponds in the years before they were built, so that chance changes are not read as effects (Impact assessment tab).
panel.unit_summary: Average over {n} assessed ponds (95% range {lo} to {hi} points of cropping intensity). By how their water looks: lined {lined}, uncertain {uncertain}, unlined {unlined} points.
panel.more_rows: The largest and smallest {n} of {total} are listed.
panel.old_footer: A comparison of places, not of years before and after: see the Impact assessment tab.

main.text: This {type_label} first held water in {year_label}, so it is treated as a new pond, but its effect on cropping around it cannot be assessed: {reason}.

This {type_label} first held water in {year_label}. In {post_text}, cropping intensity in its zone of influence was about {effect_abs} points higher than predicted had it not been built. That is an early sign of a gain: it rests on too few years, or on years in which nearly every pond of the district had already been built, to confirm.

This {type_label} first held water in {year_label}. In {post_text}, cropping intensity in its zone of influence was about {effect_abs} points lower than predicted had it not been built. That is an early sign of a loss: it rests on too few years, or on years in which nearly every pond of the district had already been built, to confirm.

This {type_label} first held water in {year_label}. Over {post_text}, cropping intensity in its zone of influence was about {effect_abs} points a year higher than predicted had it not been built. Ponds show a difference this large in the years before they were built less than one time in ten, so the gain is likely real.

This {type_label} first held water in {year_label}. Over {post_text}, cropping intensity in its zone of influence was about {effect_abs} points a year lower than predicted had it not been built. A loss this large is unusual; ask whether the pond took more cropland than its own area, or whether the zone of influence is drawn around the wrong fields.

This {type_label} first held water in {year_label}. Over {post_text}, cropping intensity in its zone of influence differed by {effect_signed} points from the prediction had it not been built, but {reason}, so the result is unsettled.

This {type_label} first held water in {year_label}. Over {post_text}, cropping intensity in its zone of influence differed by {effect_signed} points from the prediction had it not been built. That is within the range ponds show in the years before they were built, so no change can be told apart from year-to-year variation.

In {early_text}, when only its micro-watershed is left as a comparison, the difference was {early_signed} points (an early sign).

Where {type_label_plural} were built later in this district, their zones were {premium_abs} points {premium_dir} their micro-watersheds before construction, so about {corrected_signed} points may be due to the structure.
